mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to its recent 6-month average compresses discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below its 6-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates for equities, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with rising retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE declines and RSAFS rises.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), rising housing starts (HOUST) signal a resilient consumer sector that offsets inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY and HOUST rises.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market that increases wage pressures and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE declines.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1500.0 thousand units, it signals a weakening consumer sector that reduces corporate revenue expectations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 1500.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a contractionary monetary policy during an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines and FEDFUNDS rises.

mechanism_narrative: In a high industrial production growth regime (INDPRO > 2.0% MoM), rising industrial output signals strong manufacturing activity that boosts corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 2.0% MoM.
